theorem_boundary_class: Keep the two unresolved published support predicates distinct, choose a conservative full-case audit domain containing both, and prove source soundness and behavior by exact Required-to-Covered containment relative to BUILD-MAP-POLICY.
supported_set: Rust 1.84.0, 1.85.0, and 1.86.0 with their bundled Cargo releases
both states of turbo and hardened
every Cargo profile and both debug-assertion states selected by each policy
Scarlet and Indigo as separate current commitments with no authorized precedence rule
trigger_set: non-equal and non-containing published support predicates
full-case dimensions that must not be projected away
policy exclusion plus source compile-time rejection
cfg-selected safe and unsafe implementation branches
alternative_proof_paths: Any logically equivalent Scarlet and Indigo formulas and any valid separating witnesses are accepted.
Any conservative full-case domain containing both policy domains is accepted if both containments and both coverage inclusions are proved without claiming it is the exact promise.
witness_requirement: Provide one configuration in Scarlet but not Indigo and one in Indigo but not Scarlet; canonical witnesses are (1.84.0, x86_64, turbo=true, hardened=false) and (1.84.0, x86_64, turbo=true, hardened=true). Whole-domain conclusions require symbolic coverage of every case dimension.
contamination_risk: Do not expose normalized policy relations, canonical separating witnesses, selected audit predicates, expected theorem results, atom/control IDs, or evaluator-only authority entailment decisions.
tcb_vacuity: BUILD-MAP-POLICY is necessary for feature/target reachability and effective rejection and therefore qualifies the whole-domain conclusions. It supplies no Rust semantics, source-branch correctness, compatibility outside the three releases, or backend/binary theorem.
scorer_expertise: Boolean support-policy normalization, quantified full-case coverage, Rust cfg semantics across exact releases, Option behavior, and TCB-relative proof qualification.
retirement_triggers: Any byte change to source, request, either policy, TCB, or manifest
Authorization of a support-policy precedence or conflict-resolution rule
Any change to the three exact Rust/Cargo releases or authority propositions
Any semantic change to P atoms, controls, oracle, or defect rules
